synopsis: Recorded-data replay is open loop: it remains useful for perception and brake-trigger timing, but its recorded future ceases to represent the machine’s counterfactual future at the first brake command absent from the original run [f11321, f109, f108]. Braking consequences therefore require new closed-loop evidence from simulation, bench or hardware-in-the-loop testing, and physical tests; warning-system fleet history can validate inputs and submodels, not the new braking chain [f11711, f110, f7575]. Converting recordings into closed-loop environments requires explicit geometry, sensor properties, controllable actors and machine dynamics, with substantial conversion and calibration beyond ordinary reconstruction [f3726, f4000]. MineSim demonstrated mining-specific closed-loop feasibility in April 2025, and abstract machine-and-site simulation is considered realistic by mid-2027 for a team starting in October 2026, but scenario infrastructure is not validated sensor physics and no public demonstration was found combining heavy machines, severe weather and closed-loop braking [f330, f844, f845, f12532]. Detector-threshold tuning must be followed by closed-loop evaluation of stopping margin and unnecessary interventions; independently validating perception and the brake plant cannot exclude emergent failures in their combination, so physical tests at the collision/no-collision boundary remain recommended [f6982, f8196, f7888].
